summary.text: Robert Smullen was elected to the New York State Assembly on November 6, 2018, and represents a district made up of all of Hamilton County and parts of Herkimer, Fulton, Montgomery, Oneida and Otsego Counties.
His official biography says he retired from the Marine Corps as a colonel after 24 years of service.

paragraphs.text: Smullen served three combat tours in Afghanistan and at the Pentagon as a military strategist, and retired from the Marine Corps in 2015, according to his Assembly biography.
In 2003 he was appointed a White House Fellow and served at the U.S. Department of Energy.

He holds a bachelor's degree in history from The Citadel, a master's degree from Georgetown's School of Foreign Service and a master's in resource management from the Eisenhower School at National Defense University.
Before his election he was Executive Director of the Hudson River-Black River Regulating District.
The biography lists his priorities as lower taxes, fewer regulations and support for veterans and service members.
He lives on Matilda Hill Farm in Johnstown with his wife, Megan, and their four children.
